newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - March 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - March 26.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on March 26. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

President Suharto says foreign observers will not be invited to observe Indonesia's general election in May but they would be allowed to come on their own accord as observers but not to supervise the poll.

Indonesian prosecutors have asked a Jakarta court to impose the death sentence on an Indonesian man being tried for the murder his brother, an Indonesian woman and an Indian business partner in Los Angelese in the United States.
The central bank, Bank Indonesia, is confident this year's general election and next year's presidential election will not put much pressure on the country's balance of payments.

The Finance Ministry has issued a new regulation prohibiting new link-ups between two or more cigarette firms be it in the form of capital, production, marketing or management. It said cigarette firms with such arrangements have two years to adhere to the ruling.

A delegation from a group of 33 East Timorese youths met with a U.N. special envoy on Tuesday after they jumped into the Austrian embassy as part of a demonstration against Indonesia's rule in the former Portuguese colony.
